references.text: Joseph is sold to Potiphar, the captain of the guard (שַׂר הַטַּבָּחִים), the same title used in 41:12 to identify Joseph's master.
Joseph's interpretation of the dreams of the cupbearer and the baker in prison, which is the direct precursor to the cupbearer recommending Joseph to Pharaoh in 41:12.
Joseph answers Pharaoh that it is not himself but God who gives dream interpretations – a direct follow-up to the cupbearer's recommendation in verse 12.
Psalm 105:17-22 summarizes Joseph's time as a prisoner and his elevation through the ability to interpret dreams, which is relevant to the event in 41:12.
Stephen mentions in his speech how God was with Joseph and gave him wisdom and favor, including his dream interpretation mentioned in Gen 41:12.
A direct narrative connection where 40:8 establishes the principle that God gives interpretations, which 41:12 confirms in action.
A clear contrast emphasizing that only God can interpret dreams through His chosen ones, not human experts.
A strong typological parallel where both Daniel and Joseph are chosen foreign servants with God's gift of dream interpretation.
